title: Giving new leisure an available direction

captions.physics: Ending a familiar programme without pleasure
captions.energy: Delaying a trial for another moment

meaning: A small chosen step supports renewed leisure when ending an old programme leaves the wish to move together waiting indefinitely.
text: Earlier leisure can end before another form begins. Death in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes completing a habitual programme without its former pleasure. The Hanged Man in energy leans towards delaying a trial for a suitable moment or another perspective. The Chariot in emotions brings excitement about possible movement together. That response stays alive when it can receive an available direction. A permanent replacement programme is unnecessary before both may freely choose one small outing and discover how it feels today.

For example, you stop spending weekends in a large shopping centre and imagine a short walk in an old district. New plans keep awaiting a special day. **A new shared path can begin with a small available stretch.** You can choose one street and decide about continuing later. Ending the previous form requires no immediate, richer alternative. Excitement needs actual agreement and permission to change the continuation through experience, beyond promising a perfect entire day.

The difficulty is expecting a new perspective to determine every subsequent step itself. Enthusiasm survives in conversation while outings become rarer. The pause becomes another habitual programme. Perspective helps when restoring action. An unfinished larger idea permits a small experience. Both can enjoy free movement now, leaving the future unknown without making each walk completely replace the earlier way of spending time together.
